name: Random Operative Narrative Library
safeSites: a reinforced maintenance compartment with two exits and an independent air supply
a rented clinic room whose owner never asks for legal names
a mobile workshop built into an obsolete cargo vehicle
a sealed archive room hidden behind a condemned transit station
a communal kitchen and sleeping floor protected by trusted residents
a forgotten observation blister overlooking the docking ring
a machine shop whose tool inventory is better defended than its front door
an abandoned emergency shelter with a functioning water recycler
a quiet apartment registered to a person who officially died years ago
a temporary camp that can be packed and abandoned in under ten minutes
personalObjects: a scratched mechanical watch that no longer keeps local time
a paper photograph with one face carefully removed
a dented cooking pot carried through three evacuations
a child's handwritten map of a neighborhood that no longer exists
a service badge from an institution the character no longer trusts
a sealed letter addressed to someone presumed dead
a plain wedding ring worn on a cord rather than a hand
a pocket notebook containing only verified facts
a broken music player holding one surviving recording
a tiny carved animal made by an important person
a key whose original lock is gone
an old transit token from the character's home city
convictions: No person becomes disposable because an institution has lost interest in them.
Power does not erase responsibility for what someone chooses to do with it.
Consent obtained through fear, hunger, dependency, or deception is not consent.
Evidence must survive the people who would benefit from destroying it.
A copy, continuation, or altered person still has the right to define who they are.
The team comes home together unless someone knowingly chooses otherwise.
An unfamiliar body or mind is not proof of guilt.
There must always be a way to surrender without being erased.
A protected community is worth more than a clean official record.
No mission objective justifies deliberately creating helpless victims.
Promises made to the dead still shape how the living behave.
Someone must remain willing to say that the accepted procedure is wrong.
touchstones: a younger sibling who still believes the character can fix anything
a former partner who knows exactly when the character is lying
a retired mentor who taught them to document every decision
a patient they once failed and refuse to forget
a neighborhood organizer who gave them shelter without asking for repayment
a child they helped evacuate from an impossible disaster
an estranged parent who keeps sending ordinary domestic messages
a colleague whose identity was legally erased but who is still alive
a spouse who demanded that survival never become an excuse for cruelty
a friend who stayed human through an experience that changed everyone else
groupBonds: I am the person who checks that everyone has an exit before the door closes.
The team has seen what I become under pressure and chose to keep me anyway.
I hold the shared evidence archive and never alter it alone.
I promised to recover any member whose body, signal, or identity can still be found.
We survived our first operation because someone disobeyed a lethal order.
I am trusted to say when the mission has stopped being worth the cost.
The group knows the name I used before Blacklight and why I abandoned it.
I carry the emergency credentials that identify the others as people rather than property.
We share one rule: nobody negotiates away another member's autonomy.
I owe the team my life, but not my conscience.
obligations: Preserve an unaltered operational record even when Blacklight requests a cleaner version.
Provide emergency aid to civilians before securing commercially valuable salvage.
Report evidence of copied, edited, or coerced personnel to an independent witness.
Return borrowed equipment or document exactly why it could not be recovered.
Maintain a viable evacuation route whenever the team establishes a temporary site.
Attempt communication before destroying an unfamiliar intelligence that is not actively attacking.
Protect the confidentiality of medical and identity records recovered in the field.
Inform the team whenever a patron, institution, or machine requests a private concession.
Identify who benefits financially or politically from every enforcement action.
Leave enough supplies for the next survivors when abandoning a safe location.
boundaries: I will not knowingly erase, merge, or overwrite a person to make an operation easier.
I will not torture a prisoner, even when the information may save time.
I will not surrender another person's body, memories, or legal identity as payment.
I will not fire into a crowd because a target may be hiding inside it.
I will not accept an order whose author refuses to be named.
I will not use a dependent person's survival needs to force their agreement.
I will not abandon an injured person solely because recovery is inconvenient.
I will not present uncertain evidence as certainty to justify violence.
I will not allow Charles to classify silence as consent.
I will not conceal a supernatural or technological risk from the people exposed to it.
debts: I promised to recover a missing person's identity record even if their body cannot be found.
A smuggler moved my family through a closed checkpoint; one day they will ask for repayment.
I owe a medic three lives and have no idea which one they intend to collect on.
I signed responsibility for equipment that was destroyed saving civilians.
A former enemy spared me after learning we had both been deceived.
I carry a sealed data package that must be delivered without opening it.
I promised a dying witness that the responsible institution would be named publicly.
Someone falsified my credentials to keep me alive, and their own identity is now at risk.
I owe shelter to anyone carrying the phrase used by my old evacuation network.
I accepted an alien device whose maker expects a future act of translation rather than payment.
charlesSaved: overriding a security door one second before the compartment vented
sending an evacuation route that contradicted every official map
admitting that the mission briefing was wrong before anyone else would
keeping my identity record separate when the recovery system tried to merge it
calling an ordinary medical team instead of treating me as an asset
revealing that the person interrogating me was using obsolete credentials
refusing an executive order that would have left my unit behind
remembering the name of someone the institution had already deleted
forcing my suit to wake me after its own diagnostics declared me dead
giving me one honest answer when a reassuring lie would have been easier
charlesNeverAnswered: who authorized the first operation that used my name
whether the copy recovered with me was ever allowed to wake up
why my medical record contains a year I never lived through
what happened to the team assigned before ours
whether he knew the extraction route would collapse
why one version of the briefing listed me as expendable
who removed the civilian casualty estimate from the mission file
whether the voice on the emergency channel was actually him
how many times my current identity has been restored from backup
why he chose me instead of someone better qualified
secrets: The character recognizes one symbol aboard the Ar'nock vessel but does not know from where.
A former employer still considers the character's body or credentials company property.
The character once altered an evidence record to protect someone they still believe was innocent.
A recovered memory contains a private conversation the character could not have witnessed.
The character has received a message apparently sent by their own future or duplicate self.
One trusted contact has asked the character never to bring Charles near them.
The character's original extraction order listed a different Archetype.
An alien interface has responded to the character before they deliberately activated it.
The character survived an event whose official casualty list includes their name.
The character knows the location of a safe site but not whether its inhabitants remain human-adjacent.
